messages.content: You are one member of a parallel architecture inquiry. Return only the contracted JSON. Produce executable mechanisms, APIs, state transitions, and verification rules; do not propose organizational process or prose-only governance.

Evidence: 84 Claude sessions in five days manually performed environment diagnosis, repository archaeology, architecture reconstruction, research synthesis, Lean proof work, refactors, tests, memory/skill creation, and repeated failure analysis. A transcript audit counted 2,067 direct mutations versus 190 subagent dispatches and about 30% human corrections. Prior harness research specifies carrier adapters with zero substrate intelligence, append-only prompt/tool/result capture, projected memory/context, deterministic tools, governed consolidation only after results, session heartbeats, work claim/settle, and context-compaction continuity. The existing free-compute-dev seed has deterministic resolver -> context -> model edit -> apply -> test -> feedback rounds -> expensive escalation, but only one task and no autonomous intake/decomposition/fanout/tool navigation/isolation/integration/memory. The existing LISS cheapest-sufficient fabric just demonstrated 24/24 schema-verified jobs at 24.45 useful jobs/min across Gemini and GitHub Models, with OpenRouter fallback and Claude available. Future volunteer CPU/GPU endpoints can join over Tailscale. The target is a Union-owned software-production fabric that receives territories/problems and keeps observing, decomposing, executing, verifying, integrating, and learning without a Codex or Claude conversation carrying the work.

Your bounded question: Specify one implementable vertical slice that can take a real repository task from objective through cloud fanout and tool-use to a test-verified integrated patch, then learn from it.

State what is absent from the current seed, give a concrete design, and name a smallest real vertical slice.

Without these, no objective can move from intake through fanout and tool-use to a verified patch and learning without human hand-carrying each transition.","design":["Task queue as SQLite WAL table: columns (task_id UUID, parent_id, status enum(pending|claimed|settled|failed), tool_type, input_json, output_json, claimed_by, claim_expires_at, heartbeat_at). Workers claim via UPDATE WHERE status=pending AND claim_expires_at < now() LIMIT 1 RETURNING *, preventing double-claim without a lock server.","Decomposer: cheapest-sufficient model call (Gemini Flash via LISS) receives (objective, repo_snapshot_hash), returns a JSON DAG: {nodes:[{id, tool_type, input_template, depends_on:[]}]}. DAG is validated by topological sort before any node is enqueued. The decomposer output is itself a settled task node.","Worker pool: N stateless processes each polling for nodes whose depends_on are all settled. Each executes its tool deterministically (read_file, grep, apply_patch, run_tests, model_call), appends one capture record to the append-only log, then updates node status to settled or failed.","Fanout: all nodes with no unsettled dependencies are simultaneously claimable. Workers are model-agnostic; LISS selects the cheapest endpoint per tool_type and token estimate. Code-generation nodes use Gemini Flash; escalation nodes use Claude Sonnet via OpenRouter.","Settlement gate: run_tests nodes only transition to settled on exit_code==0. On failure, the parent subtask chain requeues with stderr appended to input_json. Two consecutive green runs required to guard against flaky tests.","Integration: a merge_patch node (always the final leaf) receives all apply_patch outputs in dependency order, concatenates diffs, resolves conflicts via git apply --3way, emits a single patch. Enqueued only after all sibling nodes settle.","Consolidation: a governed model_call node enqueued only after merge_patch settles — enforced by depends_on at claim time, not convention. Reads the full trace, emits a structured memory entry {pattern, files_touched, fix_type, what_failed, token_cost}, writes it to the memory store.","Context projection: each model_call node receives only files named in its input_json plus its depends_on outputs. Workers expand context lazily via logged read_file calls during their turn, keeping each call within a 32k token budget."],"firstVerticalSlice":["Input: one real GitHub issue — 'ImportError: cannot import name X from module Y' — in a repo with an existing test suite. The issue URL is the only human input.","Decomposer node runs: reads the issue body and repo file-tree hash, emits a 4-node DAG: grep_for_symbol, read_source_file, propose_edit, run_tests.","grep_for_symbol and read_source_file are independent and claimed in parallel by two workers. Each appends its (tool, input, output) record to the capture log. Elapsed: ~3 s.","propose_edit is claimed once both dependencies settle. Worker sends grep result and file content to Gemini Flash via LISS, receives a unified diff. Appends to log. Elapsed: ~8 s.","apply_patch applies the diff via git apply; run_tests executes the repo's test command. On exit 0 both settle. On failure, propose_edit requeues with test stderr appended to context.","merge_patch (pass-through for a single patch) emits the final diff and opens a draft PR via a logged GitHub API tool call.","Consolidation reads the full 6-node trace and writes one memory entry: {fix_type: moved_symbol, pattern: 'grep before proposing avoids hallucinated paths', token_cost: 1840}. Task complete."],"failureModes":["Decomposer emits a cyclic DAG — topological sort at enqueue time rejects it and requeues the decomposer with the cycle description in context, forcing corrected emission.","Worker dies mid-step and heartbeat expires — any worker re-claims the node because claim_expires_at < now(); deterministic tool calls are idempotent; model_call nodes carry full input_json so replay is safe.","run_tests passes on a flaky test then fails in CI — settlement requires two consecutive exit-0 runs with a 30-second gap; a single green is insufficient.","Consolidation fires before all patches are verified — structurally prevented: consolidation's depends_on includes merge_patch; the claim-poll check enforces this, not a runtime flag.","propose_edit hallucinates a file path — apply_patch runs git apply --check first; failure appends 'file not found: <path>' to context and requeues propose_edit with grep output as ground truth.","Context projection misses a transitive dependency — the propose_edit worker may issue read_file calls during its turn; each is logged and appended to context before the model call executes."],"successMetric":"A real ImportError issue moves from filed GitHub issue to merged PR with passing CI, full append-only tool-use trace in the capture log, and one structured memory entry persisted — zero human keystrokes after issue creation, wall-clock time under five minutes, verified across three independent runs on different repositories."}

structured_output.component: Work-claim/settle loop with append-only tool-use capture
structured_output.absentMechanism: The seed has one human-triggered linear pass: model→apply→test. Five connectives are missing: (1) queue-backed work-claim with heartbeat/TTL for autonomous pickup; (2) DAG decomposition emitting typed subtasks with dependency edges enabling safe fanout; (3) append-only per-step capture of (task_id, step_id, tool, input, output, timestamp); (4) a settlement gate withholding integration until test-verified exit-0 is recorded; (5) a governed post-settlement consolidation call that writes a memory entry. Without these, no objective can move from intake through fanout and tool-use to a verified patch and learning without human hand-carrying each transition.
design: Task queue as SQLite WAL table: columns (task_id UUID, parent_id, status enum(pending|claimed|settled|failed), tool_type, input_json, output_json, claimed_by, claim_expires_at, heartbeat_at). Workers claim via UPDATE WHERE status=pending AND claim_expires_at < now() LIMIT 1 RETURNING *, preventing double-claim without a lock server.

Decomposer: cheapest-sufficient model call (Gemini Flash via LISS) receives (objective, repo_snapshot_hash), returns a JSON DAG: {nodes:[{id, tool_type, input_template, depends_on:[]}]}. DAG is validated by topological sort before any node is enqueued. The decomposer output is itself a settled task node.

Worker pool: N stateless processes each polling for nodes whose depends_on are all settled. Each executes its tool deterministically (read_file, grep, apply_patch, run_tests, model_call), appends one capture record to the append-only log, then updates node status to settled or failed.

Fanout: all nodes with no unsettled dependencies are simultaneously claimable. Workers are model-agnostic; LISS selects the cheapest endpoint per tool_type and token estimate. Code-generation nodes use Gemini Flash; escalation nodes use Claude Sonnet via OpenRouter.

Settlement gate: run_tests nodes only transition to settled on exit_code==0. On failure, the parent subtask chain requeues with stderr appended to input_json. Two consecutive green runs required to guard against flaky tests.

Integration: a merge_patch node (always the final leaf) receives all apply_patch outputs in dependency order, concatenates diffs, resolves conflicts via git apply --3way, emits a single patch. Enqueued only after all sibling nodes settle.

Consolidation: a governed model_call node enqueued only after merge_patch settles — enforced by depends_on at claim time, not convention. Reads the full trace, emits a structured memory entry {pattern, files_touched, fix_type, what_failed, token_cost}, writes it to the memory store.

Context projection: each model_call node receives only files named in its input_json plus its depends_on outputs. Workers expand context lazily via logged read_file calls during their turn, keeping each call within a 32k token budget.
firstVerticalSlice: Input: one real GitHub issue — 'ImportError: cannot import name X from module Y' — in a repo with an existing test suite. The issue URL is the only human input.
Decomposer node runs: reads the issue body and repo file-tree hash, emits a 4-node DAG: grep_for_symbol, read_source_file, propose_edit, run_tests.
grep_for_symbol and read_source_file are independent and claimed in parallel by two workers. Each appends its (tool, input, output) record to the capture log. Elapsed: ~3 s.
propose_edit is claimed once both dependencies settle. Worker sends grep result and file content to Gemini Flash via LISS, receives a unified diff. Appends to log. Elapsed: ~8 s.
apply_patch applies the diff via git apply; run_tests executes the repo's test command. On exit 0 both settle. On failure, propose_edit requeues with test stderr appended to context.
merge_patch (pass-through for a single patch) emits the final diff and opens a draft PR via a logged GitHub API tool call.
Consolidation reads the full 6-node trace and writes one memory entry: {fix_type: moved_symbol, pattern: 'grep before proposing avoids hallucinated paths', token_cost: 1840}. Task complete.
failureModes: Decomposer emits a cyclic DAG — topological sort at enqueue time rejects it and requeues the decomposer with the cycle description in context, forcing corrected emission.

Worker dies mid-step and heartbeat expires — any worker re-claims the node because claim_expires_at < now(); deterministic tool calls are idempotent; model_call nodes carry full input_json so replay is safe.
run_tests passes on a flaky test then fails in CI — settlement requires two consecutive exit-0 runs with a 30-second gap; a single green is insufficient.
Consolidation fires before all patches are verified — structurally prevented: consolidation's depends_on includes merge_patch; the claim-poll check enforces this, not a runtime flag.
propose_edit hallucinates a file path — apply_patch runs git apply --check first; failure appends 'file not found: <path>' to context and requeues propose_edit with grep output as ground truth.
Context projection misses a transitive dependency — the propose_edit worker may issue read_file calls during its turn; each is logged and appended to context before the model call executes.
structured_output.successMetric: A real ImportError issue moves from filed GitHub issue to merged PR with passing CI, full append-only tool-use trace in the capture log, and one structured memory entry persisted — zero human keystrokes after issue creation, wall-clock time under five minutes, verified across three independent runs on different repositories.
